verdicts.why: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S3, episodes 17 to 20: Hive controls Daisy (she kills Malick, frames Lincoln and leaves to serve him) until Lash frees her in 3x20 and she goes back to S.H.I.E.L.D., then leaves at the end of 3x22. Possessed service counts, and the dataset already files Hive's group as HYDRA (T:st-hive, T:st-giyera).

Bobbi was a S.H.I.E.L.D. agent before going undercover as HYDRA's security chief. The 2x05 reveal and the 2x15 Iliad flashback show it, so S.H.I.E.L.D. goes first, then HYDRA (undercover), then S.H.I.E.L.D. again. This matches Simmons's record.

held: minor employer. Lincoln's hospital job is a single job seen in one episode (3x01), which is an open owner question. Also, the screen only says 'Cincinnati Hospital' (a news report in 3x03); 'Cincinnati Memorial Hospital' is the wiki's name.

In 7x07, stranded in the 1980s, Deke introduces Mack to his band ('I wanna introduce you to the Deke Squad'), which doubles as an unofficial S.H.I.E.L.D. unit. By 7x13 the squad has been folded into that timeline's S.H.I.E.L.D., with Deke as Director. A band counts.

Confirmed: the alias files shown on screen in 3x01 list the CIA (2008-09), NASA (2010-12) and 'Agency: MI-6'. The proposal leaves out the fourth file shown in the same shot: Samantha Potter, a special-projects consultant 'at CDC' (2013-15), which comes before the ATCU.

In S3 Andrew Garner teaches Psychology 101 at Culver University (3x02) and holds May in a Culver building in 3x07. His A twin already has Culver University, and both of a person's files must list the same groups.

Kingo stars in Howard Stark's Stark Pictures production Cosmic Queen and leaves Arishem's side for a three-picture deal with Stark Pictures. He ends at the premiere promising a sequel. He is an ongoing studio star, not a one-job hire, and Agatha's record in the same world already has Stark Pictures.

Dreykov gives Alexei an undercover Red Room mission, and Alexei grumbles on screen: 'Typical Red Room borscht. They say they care, but do they?' Later a Red Room task force comes to kill him, which is the departure already on file. This matches his main-MCU record and Dreykov's.

On Sakaar, Tony is shown reports that Pepper is acting CEO of Stark Industries in his absence. That tells on screen of his past company, so it goes first, keyed to his first title (his record's first step is episode 13, What If...? S2).

In Marvel Zombies episode 3, New Asgard's Asgardians are turned and Asgard falls. Valkyrie escapes with Kamala's group and pilots the Commodore. In episode 4 she joins their last stand and is killed. 'The Survivors' is the dataset's name for that group.

The name 'Black Widows' comes only from the wiki's plot paraphrase ('Vostokoff orders the Black Widows to take positions'). No line confirms the screen says it, and the dataset has no Widows group outside 'The Red Room'. The dataset also files this North Institute crew as The Survivors (Melina's zombie record is The Survivors from the start). So the proposal would split one crew across two names. An unsure case keeps what's there; if pursued, it is an owner call covering Melina and Alexei too.

On screen, Strange tells Earth-838's Mordo that killing their Stephen Strange was 'your ticket to getting the Sanctum, to becoming Sorcerer Supreme'. So the 838 Strange was a Master of the Mystic Arts before and alongside the Illuminati. This matches T:karl-mordo-838 (Masters of the Mystic Arts, then the Illuminati) and the Marvel Database.

Mordo introduces her on screen as 'Captain Carter: the first Avenger', which tells that she was one of Earth-838's Avengers. That past group goes first. The MCU Wiki (Avengers/Earth-838, disbanded) and the Marvel Database both list it.

held: this is already an open owner call (not_applied.json, held: 'Void variants whose home world is never shown carry no Earth', covering Nicepool, Dogpool and Ladypool). Marvel Database's Earth-TRN872 is not a home world. It is its catch-all for people pruned to the Void whose home reality is unknown (Nicepool's own page says Reality: Unknown). If the owner takes the Marvel Database number, the value is Earth-TRN872.

In TAS 'Slave Island', Cameron Hodge says on screen that Cable was a mercenary in the Leader's army until he learned the Leader was no champion of democracy, threw his wages back and took to the hills. That past service to Genosha's army goes first. The dataset already uses 'Genosha'.

In X-Men '97 episode 4, Forge tells Storm that after the war the Department of Defense helped him in exchange for building devices to neutralize mutants, and that he later left it. The Marvel Database lists the U.S. Department of Defense as mentioned in that episode. That past employer goes first, then the government job running X-Factor.

The Marvel Database files the 2055 rebel Forge of TAS 'Days of Future Past' as a separate character, Forge (Daniel) (Earth-31393). The Earth-92131 Forge's page starts at TAS S3E15 (episode 37). The dataset already files Bishop's future as Earth-31393, and Wolverine's record has no episode 11 step. Corrected value: drop the episode 11 step from A:fox-anim-forge (or give it its own Earth-31393 record); groups are unchanged.
